name: The Prediction Error Encoding Principle
higher_order_principle: PREDICTION ERROR IS THE MASTER MECHANISM OF LEARNING. Every effective instructional method works by generating prediction errors that enhance hippocampal encoding. Every ineffective method fails because it generates no prediction errors. This is the unifying principle: testing (forces prediction → often wrong → PE), generation (produces candidate answer → often wrong → PE), interleaving (disrupts category-based prediction → PE), active learning (requires prediction → frequent PE), elaborative interrogation (asks 'why?' → forces causal prediction → PE when wrong). Passive methods (rereading, highlighting, listening) generate no predictions and therefore no PE and therefore no encoding signal.
transferable_to: scientific inquiry (hypothesis testing as PE generation)

causal_links.key_evidence: Roediger & Karpicke, 2006; Bjork & Bjork, 2011; Freeman et al., 2014

high_PE_methods.testing/retrieval_practice: student generates prediction (their answer) → compared to correct answer → PE drives encoding
high_PE_methods.generation: student produces answer BEFORE being told → even wrong generation enhances subsequent encoding of correct answer
high_PE_methods.interleaving: mixing categories disrupts category-level predictions → forces discriminative processing → PE at category boundary
high_PE_methods.active_learning: student makes predictions, tests them against reality → frequent PE → enhanced encoding
high_PE_methods.Socratic_questioning: teacher asks questions that expose misconceptions → student's implicit prediction is wrong → PE

low_PE_methods.rereading: material matches what was read before → PE ≈ 0 → minimal encoding
low_PE_methods.passive_lecture: student receives information without generating predictions → minimal PE unless material is inherently surprising

parameters.neuromodulators: Dopamine (VTA → Hippocampus) signals PE magnitude. Acetylcholine enhances encoding state.
parameters.mechanism: PE triggers VTA firing → dopamine release in hippocampus → enhances LTP (persistence of memory)
parameters.interaction: This links E6 directly to T41 (Reward PE) and T17 (Novelty) — they share the dopaminergic error signal mechanism.

parameters.requirement: PE must be followed by FEEDBACK (correct answer). PE alone warns of error; feedback provides the update.
parameters.hypercorrection_effect: high-confidence errors produce larger PE when corrected → better memory for the correction than low-confidence errors

scope_conditions: PE must be 'surmountable' — if the error is too large (chaos), the brain may disengage (learned helplessness)
Feedback must be immediate or close in time to the PE for optimal binding
Emotional safety is required — high threat converts PE into stress/anxiety rather than curiosity/learning
moderators: confidence (higher confidence in wrong answer = larger PE = better learning of correction)
learner_agency (self-generated predictions produce stronger PE than observed ones)

interactions.description: E6 is the functional principle that drives the mechanism of E1.
E6 extends the core predictive processing principle (T1) to the domain of complex conceptual learning and instruction.
Learning PE (informational) and Reward PE (motivational) both utilize the midbrain dopamine system.

overall_maturity: how-plausibly (as a unified educational theory) / how-actually (as a neural mechanism)
key_references: Roediger, H. L., & Karpicke, J. D. (2006). Test-enhanced learning. Psychological Science
Bjork, E. L., & Bjork, R. A. (2011). Making things hard on yourself, but in a good way. Psychology and the Real World
Freeman, S., et al. (2014). Active learning increases student performance in science, engineering, and mathematics. PNAS
Metcalfe, J. (2017). Learning from errors. Annual Review of Psychology
